sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 (0.180.0) WebGPURenderer with WebGL 2 fallback; Rapier 0.19.3 WebAssembly; Gamepad API; Web Audio; WebRTC; AI Hub session client 1.4.0
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel-shaded 3D toy cars and circuit; thick ink edges; parchment, tangerine and mint motor-club palette
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer and AnimationClip keyframe tracks for car suspension, wheels and club flag; procedural steering, particles and camera motion
sourceInformation.audio: Code-written swing-funk music at 10% default volume, synthesized effects and engine, formant-filter Animalese-style gibberish voices; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: 1–2 player cooperative AI Hub shared-world sessions with authoritative host snapshots; standalone direct WebRTC connection codes; local couch co-op
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Chromium WebGPU, actual Rapier simulation, scripted full-run playthroughs, emulated standard gamepads, touch profiles, Web Audio signal analysis and two-page network sessions; no physical controller, listening test or real mobile hardware
sourceInformation.research: none; source interpreted from native model knowledge. Only required pinned dependencies and user-specified AI Hub integration files were fetched.

testingFeedback: Six confirmed issue classes were corrected: duplicate bundled helper declarations, exhausted-boost reactivation, minimum-charge bypass, missing Hub metadata, touch pause wiring, and device-reset recovery. Additional review corrected network input and end-state edge cases.
Two were game breaking: a bundle syntax error prevented startup, and lost graphics devices left the circuit invisible. Both were corrected.

Actual Rapier AI playthroughs collected all 288 fares across three rounds in solo and co-op. Raw WebGPU pixel-readback canaries isolated the headless graphics flag problem; two-page tests checked shared inputs and identical terminal results.

Screenshots captured before GPU presentation were least helpful: they could show an empty canvas despite initialized gameplay. State assertions, GPU readiness and pixel readback were more informative.
engineFeedback: Three.js combines procedural geometry, cel-shaded materials, native AnimationMixer tracks and WebGPU rendering without an asset pipeline.

The pinned Rapier entry point is rapier.mjs rather than the older rapier.es.js name. Headless Chromium also needed an explicit ANGLE backend; raw WebGPU canaries confirmed the launch configuration was responsible.
The lane-junction simulation, rival behavior, controller-first menus and authoritative cooperative lifecycle.
Coordinating kinematic sensor collisions and restoring presentation and textures after a graphics-device reset.
none; all game systems and graphics recovery are application code.

aiHub.name: Dodge Riot
aiHub.tagline: Four lanes. A full tank of trouble.
aiHub.description: Sweep four nested circuits, slip past oncoming rivals and zip your way into the motor club. Three escalating arcade rounds for a solo driver or a cooperative pair.
aiHub.controls: P1: arrows / A D steer, Space / W zip, Down / S brake; local P2: A D steer, W zip, S brake; pad: D-pad / stick steer, R2 zip, L2 brake, Options pause; touch: left thumb steer, right ZIP button.
